## Claims
- [source-backed] For \(v=v_{r,s,t,n}\) with \(\mathfrak S_v=s_{i^j}\), put \(a=\min(n-r-i,r-j)\), \(b=\min(i,j)\). The two displayed Schur-function sets generate \(J_v\) integrally as an ideal of \(H^\star(G/P_J,\mathbb Z)\cong\Lambda/I_{r,n-r}\), and each has \(\binom{a+b}{a}\) elements. [source-2, lines 1380-1421]
- [source-backed] The paper conjectures these two generating sets are minimal; it reports finite verification only for \(r\le4\) and \(n-r\le5\). [source-2, lines 1489-1502]
- [proved] Let \(R\) be a commutative unital ring, \(\Lambda=\bigoplus_{d\ge0}\Lambda_d\) a connected graded \(R\)-algebra (\(\Lambda_0=R\)), and \(M=\bigoplus_{d\ge N_0}M_d\) a bounded-below graded \(\Lambda\)-module. For homogeneous \(m_1,\ldots,m_t\), they generate \(M\) iff their images generate \(Q:=M/\Lambda_+M\) over \(R\). Proof: the forward implication is immediate. Conversely, induct on degree \(d\). Modulo \(\Lambda_+M\), a homogeneous \(m\in M_d\) is an \(R\)-linear combination of the \(m_i\) of degree \(d\); the difference lies in \(\sum_{e>0}\Lambda_eM_{d-e}\), whose module factors have smaller degree and hence lie in the generated submodule by induction.
- [proved] Under the preceding hypotheses, a homogeneous generating set of \(M\) is inclusion-minimal iff its image is an inclusion-minimal \(R\)-spanning set of \(Q\). Apply the previous claim to every subset obtained by deleting generators.
- [proved] If \(A\) is a quotient of \(\Lambda\), \(M\subseteq A\) is an ideal, and \(S\subseteq M\), then \(S\) generates \(M\) as an \(A\)-ideal iff it generates \(M\) as a \(\Lambda\)-module. This follows from surjectivity \(\Lambda\to A\).
- [proved] Consequently, for the integral \(J_v\), if \(Q=J_v/\Lambda_+J_v\) requires \(N=\binom{a+b}{a}\) generators as an abelian group, then each of the two \(N\)-element sets above is inclusion-minimal. This proves the conditional indecomposables reduction.
- [proved] The stronger condition \(J_v/\Lambda_+J_v\cong\mathbb Z^N\) implies the preceding generator-number condition. More generally, for nonzero \(R\), if \(Q\cong R^N\), every \(N\)-element spanning set is minimal: localizing at a maximal ideal and reducing modulo it shows that fewer than \(N\) elements cannot span.
- [proved] For a finitely generated abelian group \(Q\cong\mathbb Z^r\oplus T\), \(\mu_{\mathbb Z}(Q)=r+\max_p\dim_{\mathbb F_p}(T/pT)\). Thus torsion can increase the required number of indecomposables; rank alone does not determine it.
- [proved] Inclusion-minimal spanning sets need not have a ring-independent or even \(\mathbb Z\)-module-independent common cardinality: \(\{1\}\) and \(\{2,3\}\) are both inclusion-minimal generating sets of \(\mathbb Z/6\). Hence the abstract reduction proves inclusion-minimality of the specified sets under \(\mu_{\mathbb Z}(Q)=N\), but does not justify a general assertion that all minimal sets have equal size.
- [proved] For scalar extension defined algebraically by \(\Lambda_R=\Lambda_{\mathbb Z}\otimes_{\mathbb Z}R\) and \(M_R=M_{\mathbb Z}\otimes_{\mathbb Z}R\), one has \(M_R/(\Lambda_R)_+M_R\cong Q\otimes_{\mathbb Z}R\); right-exactness suffices, so no flatness is needed. If \(Q\cong\mathbb Z^N\), this becomes \(R^N\), giving minimality over every nonzero \(R\). If \(Q\) has torsion, base change can kill indecomposables, so integral minimality does not automatically transfer.
- [source-backed] The stronger freeness statement \(J_v/\Lambda_+J_v\cong\mathbb Z^{\binom{a+b}{a}}\) is conjectural in the source, which states that a proof had eluded the authors. [source-2, lines 1517-1552]

## Strategy
Reduce ideal minimality to indecomposables by the graded lemma, then prove the needed lower bound for \(J_v/\Lambda_+J_v\). Freeness of rank \(\binom{a+b}{a}\) would suffice.

## Gaps
The required indecomposables computation is unresolved. No supplied evidence supports extending the geometric/cohomological identifications to arbitrary coefficient rings beyond the integral type-\(A\) statement. Independent review remains outstanding.

## Next
Prove or disprove \(J_v/\Lambda_+J_v\cong\mathbb Z^{\binom{a+b}{a}}\), including torsion, for the specified \(v_{r,s,t,n}\).
